What if every promise you heard... left a thread?
A real one. Glowing. Tied from their wrist... to your heart.
Keep the promise, and it lights up like a firework. Break it...
...and it hangs there. Grey. For everyone to see. Well. For YOU to see.
You wake up. Your alarm promises, "five more minutes."
The thread snaps grey before you even sit up.
Downstairs, Mom says, "I'll drive you today." Gold. Thick. Already glowing.
[normal speaking voice, playful, mimicking a kid]
Your little brother promises he'll "clean his room THIS time."
[normal speaking voice, amused, with a small laugh]
The rules are simple. Every promise makes a thread. Big promises, thick threads. Kept ones turn to light. Broken ones turn grey... and drag.
The bus driver: "I'll wait for you!"
A billboard promises "your best summer ever." The thread goes up into the sky, and just... ends.
By lunch, you learn the first secret. Most promises aren't lies. People just... forget.
At school, it's like seeing the future.
"I'll pay you back Friday." Thin. Already sagging. You keep your money.
Ms. Bell: "I'll grade them by Monday." Twenty-eight threads, one to every desk, all still gold.
She means it. She's just tired.
At casino night, a kid swears he'll "split the winnings." The thread is already grey before the cards are dealt.
You stop trusting words. You start trusting threads.
Group projects? You pick the gold ones. Dates? Gold ones. Friends?
For about a week, your life is perfectly organised... by light.
There's a thread between you. Old. From a long time ago.
"I'll always save you a seat." You remember her saying it. In second grade.
It's still there. Still gold. Barely. Because she still saves it. Every day. And you never sit there.
You start seeing it everywhere. Not lies. Just... waiting.
Late at night, you find Dad at the kitchen table.
[normal speaking voice, quiet awe, firm and clear]
He has one thread. One. Thick as a rope. Gold. Going to every one of you.
[normal speaking voice, warm, mimicking a tired dad]
You ask him what he promised. He laughs. "That I'd take care of you."
He never said it out loud. Not once. And it's the brightest thread in the house.
You go to the bathroom, turn on the light... and look in the mirror.
You never thought to look at your OWN wrist.
[normal speaking voice, stunned, firm and clear]
"I'll start tomorrow." "I'll call Grandma." "I'll be nicer to Leo." "I'll text you back."
Most of them are grey. And they all lead... to people you love.
But one is older than all the others.
It leads to YOU. Seven years old.
Promises to yourself count too. You just never see them break.
So the next morning, you keep one.
You sit in the seat Maya saves.
And the thread between you... doesn't snap.
You call Grandma. Gold. You help Leo clean his room. He's so shocked, HIS thread bursts too.
Your wrist doesn't get lighter overnight. But it gets brighter.
And that oldest thread? You're working on it.
[normal speaking voice, warm, direct to camera]
So. If you could see every promise you've made...
[normal speaking voice, warm, direct to camera, slow]
